t:
(a) Repeal.—Section 2489 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking subsections (b) and (c). 
    (b) Conforming Amendments.—Such section is further amended—
        (1) by striking “General Authority.—(1)” and inserting “Authority to Establish Restrictions.—”; 
        (2) by striking “(2)” and inserting “(b) Limitations on Use of Authority.—”; and 
        (3) by redesignating subparagraphs (A) and (B) as paragraphs (1) and (2), respectively.

fable.w: The section only repeals two subsections of 10 U.S.C. 2489 and makes conforming heading and numbering changes. The tempting reading is that the new heading "Authority to Establish Restrictions" signals a grant of regulatory authority, but this is just a relabelled heading on existing text. Nothing here sets up a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or a right to sue.
fable.s: by striking “General Authority.—(1)” and inserting “Authority to Establish Restrictions.—”

opus.w: This section only repeals two subsections and makes conforming changes to headings and numbering. It sets up no process that brings non-federal parties into a federal decision. The heading "Authority to Establish Restrictions" might look like rulemaking authority, but the text itself grants no regulatory power and provides for no outside input.
opus.s: Section 2489 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking subsections (b) and (c).
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The new heading "Authority to Establish Restrictions" could suggest rulemaking or regulatory authority, which would count as participation.
2. **Why it fails:** This section only repeals two subsections of 10 U.S.C. 2489 and renames and renumbers what is left. The text doesn't create or require any regulation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. Whatever the underlying statute says isn't shown here.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the United States Code, specifically repealing subsections and renumbering/relabeling others. It does not establish any process for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with parties outside the government. There are no advisory committees, public comment periods, or rights to sue mentioned or created in this text.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Repeal.—Section 2489 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking subsections (b) and (c). (b) Conforming Amendments.—Such section is further amended— (1) by striking “General Authority.—(1)” and inserting “Authority to Establish Restrictions.—”; (2) by striking “(2)” and inserting “(b) Limitations on Use of Authority.—”; and (3) by redesignating subparagraphs (A) and (B) as paragraphs (1) and (2), respectively.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section amends a statute that previously contained provisions about authority, it implicitly involves some form of consultation or participation. However, the text provided is purely technical, dealing with the repeal of subsections and the renumbering/relabeling of remaining paragraphs. It does not create any new requirement for the federal government to consult with outside parties, nor does it establish any advisory bodies, comment periods, or rights to sue. It is a structural amendment to the code.
